chunks: Among them is Al-Nabigha Al-Ja'di from the Banu Amir ibn Sa'sa'a, known as Abu Laila. Abu Hatim Al-Sijistani said: Al-Nabigha Al-Ja'di was older in age than Al-Nabigha Al-Dhubyani.

key_terms.أبو حاتم السجستاني: Abu Hatim Al-Sijistani, a prominent scholar of language and poetry
key_terms.أبو ليلى: Abu Laila, the kunya (patronymic) of Al-Nabigha Al-Ja'di
key_terms.النابغة الجعدي: Al-Nabigha Al-Ja'di, a famous pre-Islamic and early Islamic poet
key_terms.بني عامر: Banu Amir, a tribe of the Arab Qays Aylan confederation

ai.seo_question: Who was Al-Nabigha Al-Ja'di and how long did he live compared to other poets?
ai.summary: This passage highlights Al-Nabigha Al-Ja'di, a renowned pre-Islamic poet of the Banu Amir tribe, as a notable example of longevity among Arabs, a theme frequently chronicled in historical and hadith literature. By citing Abu Hatim Al-Sijistani, the text underscores the scholarly tradition of verifying and comparing the lifespans of these figures, specifically distinguishing Al-Ja'di as senior to his contemporary, Al-Nabigha Al-Dhubyani. This identification serves to validate the authenticity of long-life narratives within the broader context of Islamic historiography.
